result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers state plainly that completion, satisfaction and a same-week quiz don't show better job performance, and both give the director honest wording. A is stronger on retention: it proposes a scored check about 30 days later using new scenarios, and it handles the small sample well by asking for a comparison group, naming confounds and reporting counts instead of p-values. B gives a fuller list of support metrics at 30/60/90 days, but it never re-checks what agents remember, and its metric list is a bit heavy for a 12-person team. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers say plainly that the three numbers don't show better job performance, and both give the director usable wording. B is stronger because it adds a delayed, observed check on new scenarios about 30 days after the course and explains why a comparison group matters by naming things like new tooling or seasonal ticket mix. A lists more concrete job metrics at 30/60/90 days, but it says less about later retention, and its suggested wording ('the content was learned') overclaims slightly without a pre-test.
